note: Storage P1 fixes (owner approval 2026-11-23): the six audit P1 defects in vault.ts — A-01 day-file dropped entries surface as resync conflict / restore-scan droppedEntryCount / readMemoriesForDayWithDiagnostics; A-02 CRLF files are probed and classified like LF (text normalized before hashing); A-04 native writes through writeFileInDir are verified by read-back (verifyWrittenFileContent); A-05 Registry read-modify-write uses the strict shard read (VaultRegistryShardUnreadableError / readVaultRegistryShardForUpdate) and a completed resync rebuilds corrupt Registry buckets before committing; VaultResyncScanResult carries corruptRegistryBuckets (L4 passes an empty set). Exact added / removed lines of vault.ts only. Deep-dive addition (owner approval 2026-11-23 19:53 JST): the resync rebuild of a corrupt bucket is HELD while the completed scan still has unreadable files (their records cannot be re-observed, so an incomplete scan must not finalize the rebuild); the hold surfaces in applyErrors and the corrupt shard is left untouched. Codex re-review addition (PR #68): singleRecordContentHashAtPath normalizes CRLF->LF before hashing, matching the classification-side convention (A-02), so unchanged CRLF duplicate conflicts are not misjudged as conflict-changed. Round 3 addition (owner approval 2026-11-23 22:15 JST): verifyVaultRegistryEntryBeforeWrite hashes the CRLF->LF normalized text before comparing with the stored baseline contentHash (Codex [P2] on 6de74cf: an unchanged CRLF conversation file with only mtime/size drift was repeatedly refused on save), and readAnchorFileEntry normalizes the text it reads the same way (its only consumers are parsers and the classification hash). The text returned by verifyVaultRegistryEntryBeforeWrite stays raw — the day-file merge reuses it and must preserve untouched sections byte-for-byte.

+if (!shard) throw new VaultRegistryShardUnreadableError(bucket, "shard structure is invalid");
